verbatim_definition_in_prompt.verbatim_line: Text inside quotation marks MUST be copied verbatim from ONE contiguous span of the cited JD body.
verbatim_definition_in_prompt.character_for_character_line: Exactness: every quoted string appears character-for-character in the supplied body text for its cited jd_id
explicit_prohibitions: add or remove articles or conjunctions
add or remove any word inside quotation marks
use ellipsis inside a quote to bridge them
verbatim_definition_in_prompt.interpretation: byte-identical, case-sensitive, contiguous. Capitalization is not called out separately but is implicitly covered by 'character-for-character'.

verbatim_definition_in_checker.tier_2_normalized: normalize whitespace + curly quotes + en/em dash + ellipsis + pipe-newline, then substring — case-preserving
verbatim_definition_in_checker.tier_3_case_insensitive: normalize then lowercase both sides then substring — AMBER (not RED)
verbatim_definition_in_checker.verdict_precedence_for_amber_tiers: any Tier ≥ 2 → AMBER unless RED conditions dominate

intended_contract.explicit_disagreement: The prompt says 'character-for-character' with no explicit tolerance. The checker implements graded tiers: verbatim / normalized / case-insensitive / R1 stitched / R2 terminal-punctuation. Tiers 2-5 emit AMBER, not RED — signalling 'close but not exactly verbatim'. This is intentional (AgentOps-5a/5c/5d DECISIONs) to keep telemetry informative without blocking the run.

checker_contract.normalize_function: collapses curly quotes to straight, en/em dash to hyphen, unicode ellipsis to '...', pipe-newline to newline, all whitespace to single space, trim
checker_contract.amber_emission: case-insensitive tier emits amber_reason `case-insensitive-only match for <jd_id>`

product_significance.ui_display_as_exact_quotation: acceptable in practice; the AMBER telemetry is the correct signal that the byte-exact contract was not met
product_significance.reasoning: The model quoted a fragment that begins mid-sentence in the source. English convention when quoting a fragment as a standalone line is to capitalize the sentence-start character. This is not paraphrase, grammar-repair, tense/plurality/word-count change, or content substitution. The prompt's 'character-for-character' language technically forbids this, but the AMBER tier exists in the checker precisely to flag such convention-driven divergence without blocking the run.

prompt_checker_comparison.contradiction_summary: Prompt requires char-for-char; checker implements a graded telemetry that AMBERs case-only differences. This is intentional and consistent with the checker's role (telemetry, not gate). Prior AgentOps-5a/5c DECISIONs approved the graded tier system.

selected_next_path.rationale: AMBER is doing exactly what it was designed to do: signal that a quote is close but not exactly verbatim, without blocking the run. The prompt is already clear ('character-for-character'). The single-character sentence-start capitalization is a benign English convention that models perform when quoting mid-sentence fragments. Tightening the checker to RED for this would fail runs for benign variance. Adding fuzzy / edit-distance / semantic / LLM judge is explicitly forbidden by policy. Reinforcing the prompt is low-impact and increases prompt tokens. Retention change (retain full quote text instead of 60-char snippet) is a design decision that carries privacy trade-offs; not required to conclude this diagnosis.
